data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's mechanism fails to specify the causal link by which a panel of non-experts, executing an expert-authored checklist, can 'correct a checklist item the original expert-author would have intuitively (and wrongly) marked as Pass.' If the checklist encodes the expert's process, the panel's application of it is causally downstream of the expert's knowledge. The target provides no causal mechanism for the panel to identify a *wrong* checklist item (i.e., an item that should have been marked Pass but is erroneously a Fail, or vice versa) without independent domain expertise. It asserts that 'internal panel disagreements and subsequent resolutions' correct the expert's error, but it never specifies what causal resource the non-experts draw on to determine that the checklist itself is wrong. Without this, the 'Error-Correction Trajectory' either collapses into mere compliance with a flawed checklist (which the target itself lists as a countercondition) or requires the non-experts to possess the very domain expertise they are stipulated to lack.
